subject: Private vs Dedicated: custody, commit, and sizing alternatives for Acadia Health

Thanks for the note this morning — our security/compliance folks asked a couple of follow-ups after the demo: specifically they want a clear comparison between a Private (customer-managed VPC/on-prem) deployment vs Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) for our PHI workloads. - Data custody: what leaves Acadia, what stays, auditability (logs/retention)
- Commitment/financial: minimums, burst options, escape hatches
- Sizing: how many GPUs for 99th p95 latency SLA for inference and a reasonable runway for pilot-to-Prod

Can you put together a short write-up comparing those two options with a recommended path for a 6–12 month pilot? We also need a copy of the MPA with highlighted clauses (we shared an internal redline separately).

Beth —

Thanks for the note and the detailed questions. I've pulled together a concise comparison and a recommended pilot path below. I added pricing/commitment bullets at the end; engineering will follow up with exact GPU counts once we confirm QPS and model family.

Summary (short):
- Private (VPC/on-prem): maximum data custody & control, longer lead time (4–10 weeks), higher ops overhead for Acadia, ideal if regulatory rules mandate zero egress or air-gapped processing. Best if you need HSM/KMS fully on-prem and full audit chain inside your network.
- Dedicated (Redwood Reserved): faster onboarding (1–2 weeks), predictable monthly committed GPUs, Redwood manages runtime, we provide SOC2 artifacts and detailed audit logs. We support tenant isolation and strict access controls; data can be restricted by policy to not be used for model training.

Pilot recommendation (6 months): start on Dedicated with a committed baseline that meets your peak 95th% latency target, and reserve an agreed burst band; if during pilot you require on-prem custody, transition plan to Private with a 4–8 week on-prem packaging window. This hybrid path minimizes time-to-value while preserving an escape hatch.

Key comparison table (short bullets):
- Data custody: Private = full custody; Dedicated = data flows through Redwood infra but can be isolated + retention controls.
- SLA & latency: both can meet 200–300ms p95 for small generative models with appropriate GPU choices; Dedicated provides easier autoscaling.
- Procurement: Private is a platform license + deployment fee + infra (customer) costs; Dedicated is reserved GPU spend + monthly Redwood platform fee.
- Onboarding effort: Private > Dedicated.
- Audit evidence: Redwood provides SOC2, access logs, and deployment-level audit bundles; Private can produce on-prem logs under your control.

Attachments: I attached a draft MPA with our standard platform PSC highlighted and an initial sizing workbook (sizing_estimate_v1.xlsx).

Next steps: can procurement confirm typical QPS and target model family (Llama2-70B quantized or Llama2-13B) so we can do a short sizing pass?

Thanks — Soojin

Hi all — quick sizing pass based on the assumptions (pilot QPS 6 sustained / 12 peak, p95 <300ms):

Scenario A — Llama2-13B quantized (q4f16-ish runtime)
- Recommended Dedicated: 4x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs in a reserved pool (baseline), with autoscale to 8 GPUs for peak. Baseline supports ~6 sustained QPS given batching and KV caching, p95 ~180–220ms.
- Commit suggestion: reserve 4 GPUs (monthly commit) + 50% burst band (metered). If they commit 12-months we can reduce unit pricing by ~15%.
- Private: 4x A100-80GB on-prem node(s) with identical runtime; expect 4–6 week provisioning + network/security testing. Ops lift: Acadia-run infra + Redwood on-prem agent install.

Scenario B — Llama2-70B quantized (int8 / 4-bit mixed)
- Recommended Dedicated: 8x H100-80GB equivalent (or 16x A100-80GB equivalents across tiled nodes) baseline, autoscale to 12 for peaks. This yields p95 ~250–320ms depending on prompt length; recommend guardrail prompting to reduce context windows for latency.
- Commit suggestion: reserve 8 GPUs baseline; offer burst to 12 with metered overage. Private: expect 8–12 week procurement + testing; larger capital + rack footprint.

Operational notes (both):
- Auditability: Dedicated provides per-request audit logs and token-level retention controls; we can export log bundles to Acadia S3 nightly. Private gives native custody — logs remain inside customer network.
- Migration path: start Dedicated with a 3-month checkpoint review; if strict custody required, migrate to Private in a 4–8 week window with validated infra spec.
- Example cost anchors (very rough): Dedicated monthly committed cost (4x A100 equiv) = ~$55k/mo platform + GPU run charge; 8x H100 equiv = ~$135k/mo committed. Private upfront packaging + integration ~ $120k–$250k depending on HSM/KMS and on-site work. We will refine after QPS + model prompt length.

I'll attach a quick sizing_estimate_v1.xlsx in the reply with the per-GPU throughput assumptions. Priyom — please sanity-check the burst economics and the 15% larger discount tier for 12-month commit.

-Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

Beth —

Thanks again for the request. Per our internal sizing pass, attached is a concise recommendation and two concrete pilot configurations keyed to the two model families you mentioned. Highlights:

Pilot A (fast-to-value, Dedicated, Llama2-13B)
- Baseline: reserve 4 A100-equivalent GPUs (supports ~6 sustained QPS; p95 ~200ms).
- Burst: metered up to 8 GPUs for peaks.
- Onboarding: ~1–2 weeks; SOC2 evidence + audit log export available.
- Commit: monthly reserved billing; 3-month pilot, option to convert to 12-month commit with discount.

Pilot B (higher-quality, hybrid path starting Dedicated then Private, Llama2-70B)
- Baseline: reserve 8 H100-equivalent GPUs (p95 in the 250–320ms range depending on prompt size).
- Transition: if custody constraints trigger, we can package an on-prem deployment for Acadia (8–12 week runway).

Next asks from your side so we can finalize numbers:
1) Confirm target prompt/context window (tokens) and expected avg token generation per request.
2) Confirm whether Acadia requires HSM-backed KMS on day 1 for the pilot.
3) Procurement: do you have an internal budget cadence for a commit conversion to 12 months?

I've attached the sizing_estimate_v1.xlsx with the per-GPU throughput table and the draft MPA with highlighted clauses we think matter for custody/retention. If you'd like, we can do a 30-min call next week to walk procurement/security through the table.

Best —
